extracted.intended_audience: OSHA rulemakers, agency staff, regulated entities, labor and industry stakeholders, administrative law attorneys, and members of the public who participate in OSHA rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules governing how the Assistant Secretary and OSHA must conduct proceedings to promulgate, modify, or revoke occupational safety or health standards, including petitions, notices, objections, hearings, emergency standards, presiding officer powers, record certification, and decision timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This part sets forth rules of procedure for promulgating, modifying, or revoking occupational safety or health standards under section 6(b) of the Act to provide for single proceedings, assure uniformity of standards, and avoid needless multiplicity of rulemaking proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides rulemaking to be consolidated where appropriate across statutes listed in §1911.2(d); intended to promote uniformity and efficiency in setting standards enforceable under several statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Key terms as used in this part: 'Assistant Secretary' means the Assistant Secretary of Labor for Occupational Safety and Health; 'Act' means the Williams-Steiger Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970; 'Standard' means an occupational safety and health standard requiring conditions or practices reasonably necessary or appropriate to provide safe or healthful employment; 'Particular statute' lists statutes of particular application (Walsh-Healey, Service Contract Act, Construction Safety Act, Longshoremen's Act, National Foundation on Arts and Humanities Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions control interpretation and application of the procedural rules throughout the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content and filing (§1911.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may file a written petition with the Assistant Secretary for promulgation, modification, or revocation of a standard; the petition should include or be accompanied by the proposed rule desired and a statement of the reasons therefor and intended effect thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be submitted to the specified OSHA address. Practical compliance involves drafting a proposed rule text plus a clear statement of reasons and intended effects to allow consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to prescribe additional or alternative procedures (§1911.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary may, upon reasonable notice to interested persons, prescribe additional or alternative procedural requirements in any particular proceeding to expedite the proceeding, to provide greater procedural protection when necessary or appropriate, or for any other good cause consistent with applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flexibility in tailoring procedure to case-specific needs; agencies may shorten or expand procedures when justified by expedition, protection of interests, or other legally consistent reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor changes — good cause finding (§1911.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b) permits making minor rules or amendments in which the public is not particularly interested without the notice and public procedure otherwise required; whenever such a minor rule or amendment is adopted, it shall incorporate a finding of good cause for not providing notice and public procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor amendments may bypass standard notice/comment if a documented 'good cause' finding is included in the rulemaking record explaining why notice/comment are unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committee consultation and submission of factual information (§1911.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary may request recommendations of an advisory committee appointed under section 7 or other statutory authority; the Assistant Secretary shall submit to the committee any proposal (his or HEW's) together with all pertinent factual information available, including results of research, demonstrations, and experiments; the committee shall submit recommendations within a period prescribed by the Assistant Secretary, not to exceed 270 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used, advisory committees must receive the proposal plus all pertinent factual information; committee timelines are capped at 270 days unless a different period is prescribed; agencies should provide complete factual records for informed committee recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed rulemaking contents and timing (§1911.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall publish a notice of proposed rulemaking in the Federal Register (within 60 days after advisory committee recommendations or expiration). The notice must include: (1) the terms of the proposed rule; (2) a reference to section 6(b) and any applicable particular statute; (3) an invitation to interested persons to submit written data, views, and arguments within 30 days (available for public inspection except where disclosure is prohibited); (4) either the time and place of an informal hearing (no earlier than 10 days after the comment period ends) or information that interested persons may file objections within 30 days and request an informal hearing; (5) any other appropriate provisions regarding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical timelines: publication within 60 days after advisory committee action (if applicable); 30-day public comment period; hearings (if scheduled) held not earlier than 10 days after the comment period. Notices must identify legal authority and provide access to submissions for public inspection, subject to legal confidentiality limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection submission requirements (§1911.11(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to a proposed rule under paragraph (b) must: (1) include the name and address of the objector; (2) be postmarked on or before the 30th day after publication of the notice; (3) specify with particularity the provision objected to and state the grounds; (4) state and number each objection separately; and (5) be accompanied by a summary of the evidence proposed to be adduced at the requested hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections that fail to meet these requirements risk being disregarded; objectors should prepare numbered, particularized objections with an evidence summary and ensure timely postmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of informal hearing content and timing (§1911.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the last day for filing objections, if objections are filed in substantial compliance, the Assistant Secretary shall (and otherwise may) publish a notice of informal hearing containing: (1) time, place, and nature of the hearing; (2) reference to the authority; (3) specification of the provisions of the proposed rule objected to and on which hearing requested; (4) specification of the issues to be heard (including at least all issues raised by proper objections); (5) requirement to file an intention to appear with a statement of position and evidence to be adduced; (6) designation of a presiding officer; (7) any other appropriate provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice frames the hearing scope and participant obligations (intent to appear, statement of issues and evidence). Agencies must specify issues and objected provisions so hearings are focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to participate in hearings (§1911.11(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any objector requesting a hearing on a proposed rule, and any interested person who files a proper intention to appear, shall be entitled to participate at a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is available to objectors who follow objection/hearing request procedures and to interested persons who properly file intentions to appear; compliance with notice requirements is necessary to preserve participation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency standards procedures and timelines (§1911.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an emergency standard is published under section 6(c), the Assistant Secretary must commence a proceeding under section 6(b) and the emergency standard shall serve as a proposed rule; the notice of proposed rulemaking shall give notice of any appropriate subsidiary proposals. An emergency standard is considered issued when officially filed in the Office of the Federal Register (used to determine timeliness of judicial review petitions). If the Assistant Secretary consults an advisory committee, interested persons must be afforded an opportunity to inspect and copy committee recommendations before hearings or before the end of the comment period when a hearing is not initially noticed. Section 6(c) requires that any standard promulgated after an emergency standard must be issued following the rulemaking proceeding within 6 months after publication of the emergency standard, and the proceeding shall be expedited as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency standards trigger expedited procedural obligations: they operate as proposed rules immediately on filing; agencies have 6 months to finalize following required proceedings; advisory committee materials must be made available in a reasonable time before hearings or comment deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of hearings — informality and evidentiary expectations (§1911.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are intended to be informal (legislative in type) rather than formal rulemaking; section 6(b)(3) provides for hearings on objections and determinations of the Secretary are conclusive if supported by substantial evidence in the record as a whole. Oral hearings are legislative in type, but fairness may require cross-examination on crucial issues; the presiding officer is empowered to permit cross-examination. Additional requirements: presiding officer shall be a hearing examiner appointed under 5 U.S.C. 3105; presiding officer shall provide opportunity for cross-examination on crucial issues; hearings shall be reported verbatim and transcripts made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although informal, hearings must create a record adequate for a substantial-evidence review if applicable; agencies should ensure hearing procedures (including potential cross-examination and verbatim transcripts) preserve a sufficiently developed record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the presiding officer (§1911.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer has powers necessary or appropriate to conduct a fair and full hearing, including: (a) regulate the course of proceedings; (b) dispose of procedural requests and objections; (c) confine presentations to issues specified in the notice or to matters pertinent to the proposed rule; (d) regulate conduct of those present; (e) in his discretion, permit cross-examination of any witness; (f) take official notice of material facts not appearing in the evidence, so long as parties may, on timely request, show the contrary; (g) in his discretion, keep the record open for a reasonable, stated time to receive written recommendations and additional data, views, and arguments from participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer controls scope and fairness of the hearing, may allow limited cross-examination, may take official notice (subject to opportunity to rebut), and may keep the record open to allow additional submissions; parties should monitor and comply with presiding officer directions and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of the hearing record (§1911.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of oral presentations, the transcript, together with written submissions on the proposed rule, exhibits filed during the hearing, and all posthearing comments, recommendations, and supporting reasons shall be certified by the presiding officer to the Assistant Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certified record comprises the verbatim transcript and all written materials and exhibits; certification by the presiding officer transmits the complete hearing record for the Assistant Secretary's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timing, considerations, and statement of basis and purpose (§1911.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the expiration of the period for submission of written data/views/arguments on a proposed rule on which no hearing is held, or within 60 days after certification of the record of a hearing, the Assistant Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register either an appropriate rule promulgating, modifying, or revoking a standard, or a determination that such a rule should not be issued. The action shall be taken after consideration of all relevant matter presented. A determination not to issue may invite additional data/views/arguments, in which event a rule or determination shall be made within 60 days after the end of the additional comment period. Any rule adopted shall incorporate a concise general statement of its basis and purpose (not necessarily detailed findings), showing the significant issues faced and articulating the rationale. Rules or determinations are considered issued when officially filed in the Office of the Federal Register (used to determine timeliness of petitions for judicial review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key timing: 60-day decision clock after comment period or certification. Decisions must reflect consideration of all relevant record material and include a concise statement of basis and purpose explaining key issues and rationale. Agencies may solicit additional comments before finalizing and must meet subsequent 60-day deadlines. Official filing date governs judicial review timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committee advice on disposition (§1911.18(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an advisory committee has been consulted, the Assistant Secretary may seek the committee's advice as to the disposition of the proceeding; the committee's advice shall be written recommendations submitted within a prescribed period. When recommendations appear in the transcript of a committee meeting, they shall be summary in form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committee input on final disposition must be in writing within prescribed timeframes; transcribed oral recommendations may be summarized. Agencies should document committee advice in the record.
